对话 1 你身上那个橙色的东西是什么电脑屏幕？
Conversation 1 What's that orange thing on your computer screen?
这是我昨天买的东西。
It's something I bought yesterday.
它是一张阻挡蓝光的塑料片。
It's a plastic sheet that blocks blue light.
我有一个用来遮盖我的手机屏幕也是如此。
I have one that I use to cover my phone screen too.
蓝光包括自然光，但也包括包括非自然光。
Blue light includes natural light, but it also includes light that isn't natural.
例如，通过电脑、电话、电视和其他电子设备。
For example, from computers, phones, televisions, and other electronic devices.
蓝光是有害的，这就是为什么你想阻止它吗？
So blue light is harmful and that's why you want to block it?
事情没那么简单。
It isn't that simple.
蓝光不一定对我们有害。
Blue light isn't necessarily bad for us.
事实上，我们在每天都要保持健康。
In fact, we need blue light during the day to be healthy.
但过多的蓝光，尤其是来自电子产品设备可能会削弱我们的视力，使我们更难睡着。
But too much blue light, especially from electronic devices, can harm our health by weakening our vision and making it harder for us to fall asleep.
睡眠不足会导致各种健康问题。
And poor sleep can cause all sorts of health problems.
我不太确定睡眠是否正如人们常说的那样，它很重要。
I'm not so sure that sleep is nearly as important as people always say it is.
我已经好几个月没有睡够了，因为我有太多工作要做。
I haven't slept enough in months because I have too much work to do.
我感觉很好。
And I feel fine.
我的大部分朋友们。
And it's the same for most of my friends.
睡眠不足可能是老年人的一个问题人，但年轻人肯定能应付晚夜晚。
Poor sleep might be a problem for older people, but surely young people can handle late nights.
嗯，我读过的研究表明睡眠可能比我们想象的还要重要，睡眠不足可能会导致导致肥胖和心脏病等严重健康问题疾病。
Well, the research I've read shows that sleep is probably even more important than we thought, and that not having enough sleep can contribute to serious health problems, like obesity and heart disease.
电子产品发出的所有人造蓝光设备意味着我们必须更加努力睡得好。
And all the artificial blue light from electronic devices means we have to try harder to sleep well.
也许你是对的。
Maybe you're right.
我经常晚上玩电脑到很晚，这可能就是我睡眠不足的原因。
I'm on my computer very late most nights, and that's probably why I don't sleep enough.
关于你刚才听到的对话。
on the conversation you have just heard.
小时候你知道什么工作吗？长大后你想做什么？
As a kid, did you know what job you wanted to do when you grew up?
不，我没有。
No, I didn't.
每次大人问我，我都感到恶心当我长大了。
And I got sick every time adults asked me what I wanted to be when I grew up.
我也是一样，我很累有 10 个人问过这个问题岁的女儿。
It's the same with me, and I'm tired of people asking that question of my 10 -year-old daughter.
我女儿的回答通常是篮球运动员、流行音乐歌手、机械工程师。
My daughter's stock answers are basketball player, pop singer, mechanical engineer.
成年人喜欢最后一个，因为它是理智与雄心的完美结合。
Adults love that last one, as it's the perfect mix of the sensible and the ambitious.
当我女儿还小的时候，说她想成为我所喜爱的云彩。
When she was much younger, my daughter used to say she wanted to be queen of the clouds, which I loved.
我喜欢这样的目标设定方式看到孩子们从他们无限的想象力。
That's the kind of goal-setting I like to see in children, springing from their boundless imaginations.
是的，我们成年人可能会很乏味，我们对现实的需求有限，教导一种非常悲观的成年人形象，无论我们的孩子的未来如何，都必须从工作角度来看。
Yes, we grown-ups can be tedious and limiting in our need for reality, and we teach a very gloomy image of adulthood, that whatever our children's future holds, it must be seen within the context of a job.
真是太让人难以忍受、太无趣了。
How utterly overwhelming and dull.
当人们问我儿子想要什么时等他长大了，我克制住说“嘿，回来吧”的冲动我孩子的梦想。
When people ask my son what he wants to be when he grows up, I have to swallow the urge to say, hey, back off my kid's dreams.
我们不能否认青少年有计划完成后再做某事学校，家长们也有权希望不仅仅是每天花 10 个小时玩电脑游戏。
We can't dismiss the idea that teenagers have to plan to do something after they finish school, and parents are entitled to hope it's more than simply spending 10 hours a day playing computer games.
但要问的是，你想成为什么？
But asking, what do you want to be?
不会让孩子充实的生活，反而会导致错误的期望并且很有可能会失望。
isn't going to lead a child to a fulfilled life, rather it leads to false expectations and a high chance of disappointment.
确切地。
Exactly.
我们应该帮助我们的孩子理解谁是的，即使这意味着放手我们认为他们应该是谁。
We should be helping our kids understand who they are, even if that means letting go of who we think they should be.
